given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Loans due 2026-03-16 are checked on 03-17, so 'before today' is set up. Nothing sets up the UTC part, because the test clock hands over plain date strings.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The loans start with no reminders and the job runs once, so the no-reminder case is the one exercised.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: `fakeNotifications.sent` must contain the exact memberId, loanId and dueOn for both loans, with length 2.
The reminders table must hold exactly the two loan ids.
B1 selects only `loan_id`, never `sent_on`, so recording the due date instead of today would pass. Only B3's test (line 103) pins `sent_on` to 2026-03-17.
B3 covers it: a refused loan gets no recorded reminder, which would fail if recording came first. The mutants.json 'not mutated' entry says the same.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice on the same day, so loan1 already has a reminder on the second run.
loan2 is overdue and then returned through the API before the job runs.
The third loan is due exactly on today (03-17), which covers the boundary.

then.why: `sent` must match a one-element array holding only loan1. A resend on the second run, or a send for the returned or not-yet-due loan, would change that.

given.why: `refuseFor(loan1, ...)` makes the fake return a refused result.
B5 shows that a failed connection becomes a refused result. The service test only ever sees that same refused result.

then.why: The reminders table must equal only loan2's row, so a row for loan1 would fail.

then.part: logs `reminder.failed` at `warn` with `loanId` and the refusal's `error`
then.why: `toContainEqual` matches the exact level, event and fields, including the loanId and the refusal's reason.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan1 is lent first and refused, and loan2 must still be sent and recorded. Stopping the run after the refusal would fail this.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, two accepted and one refused, and the job runs to completion.

then.why: The last log entry must equal level info, event reminders.finished and fields `{ sent: 2, failed: 1 }`.

given.why: The tests call `sendOverdueReminder` directly with a reminder.

then.why: The recorded request must have method POST and path /notifications, and the handler is built on the NOTIFY_URL base.

then.part: with JSON `{ memberId, template: loan-overdue, data: { loanId, dueOn } }`
then.why: The content-type must be application/json and the body must equal the exact shape, so a renamed key or a different template would fail.
202, 200 and 204 are each asserted as accepted, so a check for 200 only would fail.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 must give a refused result whose reason contains '400'.

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: A network error must give a refused result whose reason contains 'unreachable'.
